answer: A ridge line of fire-watch towers gives each agent one tower. At dawn the agent climbs up, reads the brass wind dial, and encodes the reading with a personal cipher built from a kernel phrase in a bound logbook. The slip goes into a locked box at the tower base. An inspector opens the box, decodes the slip with the registered kernel phrase, and checks it against the dial. A copied cipher or guessed reading costs the tower for a season. A thousand fake names need a thousand dawn climbs and a thousand cipher books with readings that match the dial.
